newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean blue chips end weak on foreign selling.
newsitem.headline: Chilean blue chips end weak on foreign selling.

text.p: Chilean blue chips ended lower in erratic trade with the market dominated by nervousness over rising U.S. long term interest rates, said dealers.
The bolsa is expected to open steady, although stocks are likely to tilt lower later if Wall Street's jitters continue, they said.
"The focus will continue on ADR-denominated stocks," said Nicolas Allende, a trader at ING Barings.
The 40-share index ended down 0.86 percent at 112.06 points. The general index lost 0.57 percent to 5,225.7 points.
Turnover swelled to 14 billion pesos from 11 billion pesos Tuesday with the high volume reflecting a wave of sales by foreign players, said traders.
Traders reported selective buying from pension funds, Chile's largest institutional investors.
Risers included drug-maker LabChile on talk the company has signed a new distribution agreement which will boost its range of products on sale in Chile, they said.
"This deal should help the company tune more closely to the market's needs," said one trader.
Electricity shares closed lower on continued sales by pension funds who are seeking to diversify into higher growth stocks including the retail sector.
The funds were net sellers of power shares in the first two months of the year and this is likely to be repeated in March, said dealers.
Enersis lost 2.15 percent to 250-1/2 pesos, while Endesa shed 0.6 percent to 247 pesos.
